anomalies.observed: The servo power rail (D2 cathode, feeding J3 pin 2 and J8 pin 2) carries only three 100 uF bulk capacitors, C1, C3 and C4, plus an additional 1 kOhm resistor R16 connected from that rail to GND (drawn immediately beside C1). anomalies.expected: Per the spec, the servo power rail downstream of D2 should be backed by four 100 uF bulk capacitors (C1-C4) and nothing else; a 1 kOhm shunt to ground is not part of that buffering network and continuously loads the rail.

evidence.quote: a second diode D2 (PMEG3030EP ...) feeds a dedicated servo power rail backed by four 100 uF capacitors (C1-C4) before reaching J3/J8 pin 2
C1-C4 | 100 uF x 4 | Bulk capacitance on the servo power rail (downstream of D2), buffering the high inrush current of PWM servos.
R16 / 1k (vertical resistor from the D2-cathode servo-rail node to GND, adjacent to C1 100u); only C1 100u, C3 100u, C4 100u are drawn on the rail

anomalies.impact: The rail has ~300 uF of bulk capacitance instead of the intended 400 uF, and the 1 kOhm resistor permanently draws about 5 mA from the servo/+5V supply. This reduces the inrush buffering the capacitor bank was designed to provide for PWM servos and adds a continuous parasitic load (battery drain when the board is battery-powered).

parsed.summary: One deviation from the stated design was found on the servo power rail: an extra 1 kOhm resistor R16 shunts the D2-fed servo rail to ground and only three of the specified four 100 uF bulk capacitors (C1, C3, C4) are present.
